title: Genetic transformation of filamentous fungi by _Agrobacterium tumefaciens_
protocol: Add a single colony of _A. tumefaciens_ AGL1 to 20 ml LB medium.
Grow overnight on a rotary shaker at 28°C and 150 rpm.
Inoculate 1 liter LB medium with 5 - 10 ml of fresh overnight culture.
Shake well at 28°C in a rotary shaker at 200 rpm until OD600 reaches 0.5 to 0.9.
Chill the flask on ice for 15 min.
Pellet cells in a sterile centrifuge tube at 4000 x g for 10 min at 4°C.
Wash pellet twice in 100 ml of cold distilled water and centrifuge at 4000 x g for 10 min at 4°C.
Remove and discard supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellet in 20 ml of cold 10% glycerol.
Centrifuge at 4000 x g for 10 min at 4°C.
Remove and discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in a final volume of 2 - 3 ml of cold 10% glycerol.
Aliquot competent cells into 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tubes (45 μl tube-1).
Place aliquots in liquid nitrogen until frozen.
Store frozen aliquots at -70°C for up to 2 years.
Place LB medium in a 28°C water bath.
Place selective plates at 28°C for 1 hour.
Place electroporation cuvettes and microcentrifuge tubes on ice.
Thaw electrocompetent cells of A. tumefaciens on ice (about 10 min).
Mix cells by flicking the tube gently.
Transfer 40 μl of cell suspension to a cooled microcentrifuge tube.
Add 1 μl of plasmid solution containing 10 - 100 pg plasmid DNA and mix gently.
Carefully transfer the cell/DNA mixture into a chilled cuvette without introducing bubbles.
Ensure the suspension deposits along the bottom of the cuvette.
Electroporate using conditions: Voltage 1.8 kV, shunt resistor 200 Ω, capacitor 25 μF.
Add 800 μl of LB medium pre-heated to 28°C to the cuvette after pulse delivery.
Mix by inverting the cuvette twice and transfer contents to a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Incubate without shaking at 28°C for 3 hours.
Spread 100 μl of cell suspension onto LB agar medium containing appropriate antibiotics.
Incubate at 28°C for approximately 48 hours until colonies appear.
Cut cellophane membranes into circles of 9.5 cm diameter.
Place a stack of cellophane membranes interlaced with filter paper strips into a glass Petri dish.
Fill the Petri dish with distilled water and autoclave for 15 minutes at 121°C.
Moisten the external supports with distilled water.
Push the cover glass gently onto the counting chamber from the front.
Place a drop of diluted spore suspension into the counting chamber covered by the cover glass.
Place the counting chamber under a light microscope.
Select an appropriate magnification.
Count spores in 4 small squares.
Calculate the spore concentration using the formula: Spores ml-1 = total spore count in 4 small squares x 2500 x dilution factor.
Plate fungal spores on an appropriate agar medium containing a dilution series of hygromycin from 50 to 300 μg/ml.
Select the lowest concentration at which no growth occurs for transformation.
Inoculate _G. roseum_ onto PDA agar.
Incubate for 20 days at 24°C.
Wash spores from one Petri dish with 3 ml of sterile tap water.
Release the spores gently from mycelium using a Drigalski spatula.
Collect the spore suspension and determine spore concentration as described in BOX3.
Adjust spore density to 10^7 spores/ml with sterile tap water.
Store spore suspensions for transformation experiments at 4°C for no more than 50 hours.
Inoculate 10 ml of LB medium in a 100 ml Erlenmeyer flask containing appropriate antibiotics with a single colony of _A. tumefacies_ carrying a transformation vector.
Grow the strain at 28°C on a rotary shaker at 200 rpm until the OD600 reaches 0.5 to 0.9.

Supplement the growth medium with kanamycin, rifampicin, and carbenicillin at 50 μg/ml, 50 μg/ml, and 25 μg/ml respectively for selection of _A. tumefaciens_ carrying Ti-plasmid pTiBo542ΔT and any binary vector from the list shown in Table 1.
Centrifuge 5 ml of the culture in a sterile 15 ml centrifuge tube at 4000 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Decant the supernatant as soon as the rotor stops.
Add 1 ml IM to the cell pellet; pipet up and down or vortex gently until cells are uniformly resuspended.
Transfer the mixture to a 2 ml microcentrifuge tube and centrifuge at 4000 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Wash the cells a second time by resuspending in 500 μl IM using the same technique.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 4000 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Resuspend the bacterial pellet in 150 μl of IM.
Dilute bacterial cells to OD600 = 0.15 with IM supplemented with 200 μM acetosyringone.
Grow cells for 8-12 hours with vigorous aeration in a 100 ml Erlenmeyer flask at 28°C until the cells reach OD600 = 0.3.
Prepare a 1:1 mixture of the fungal spore suspension at 10^7 ml^-1 and the induced A. tumefaciens culture.
Spread the mixture onto the surface of a cellophane sheet placed on an IM agar plate supplemented with 200 μM acetosyringone.
Incubate the plates for 60 hours at 23°C.
Transfer the cellophane membranes onto selection plates containing 200 μM cefotaxime and hygromycin B after co-cultivation.
Transfer colonies of transformants onto fresh selection plates containing the same antibiotics after 7-10 days.
